title: ALMA detects molecular gas in the halo of the powerful radio galaxy TXS 0828+193
question: What is the origin of the luminous off-source CO(3-2) emitting region near the z=2.57 radio galaxy TXS 0828+193, and are there additional CO-emitting companion galaxies or cold gas clouds in its overdense environment?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms: 6.9 uJy beam^-1; line rms: 0.11-0.12 mJy beam^-1 per 72.6 km s^-1 channel (at primary beam centre)

what.value: IRAM PdBI CO(3-2) observations, beam size (5.3'' x 4.6''), channel rms (~0.3 mJy beam^-1 per 30 km s^-1 channel), and SW1/SW2 component properties

evidence.quote: (cite: 2009MNRAS.395L..16N) studied the molecular gas of TXS 0828+193 through observation of the CO(3–2) line using the IRAM PdBI.

evidence.loc: CO(3–2) line emission in TXS 0828+193 and companion #1
evidence.quote: In order to test this option, we tapered the ALMA data to the beam of the PdBI data ($5.3\ensuremath{''}\times4.6\ensuremath{''}$).

what.value: Spitzer IRAC 3.6 um and 4.5 um photometry, data reduction, completeness limits, and colour criterion from the CARLA program

evidence.loc: Multi-wavelength properties of the companion candidates
evidence.quote: The flux densities of companion #1 at $3.6\,\mu \rm m$ and $4.5\,\mu \rm m$ are $1.37\pm0.24\,\mu\rm Jy$ and $3.40\pm0.19\,\mu\rm Jy$ (for details about the data reduction and photometry see (cite: 2013ApJ...769...79W)).

evidence.loc: Multi-wavelength properties of the companion candidates
evidence.quote: According to (cite: 2013ApJ...769...79W) for a source to be real and considered as a cluster member, its flux density needs to be above the completeness limit in both IRAC bands ($3.45\,\mu\rm Jy$ at $3.6\,\mu \rm m$ and $2.55\,\mu\rm Jy$ at $4.5\,\mu\rm m$), and satisfy the colour criterion of $[3.6]-[4.5]>-0.1$.

recipe.goal: Image 100 GHz continuum and measure continuum flux densities
recipe.method: Image the continuum with TCLEAN in CASA using natural weighting while excluding the spectral window containing line emission (96.53-97.17 GHz), clean to 0.01 mJy threshold, and apply primary beam correction; report 3-sigma upper limits from the primary beam corrected cube for non-detections.

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum and image the CO(3-2) line cube
recipe.method: Fit the continuum using line-free channels of every spectral window and subtract it in the uv-plane using UVCONTSUB in CASA, then image the line cube with TCLEAN using natural weighting and 6-channel binning (72.6 km s^-1), and apply primary beam correction. Also produce a uv-tapered cube matching the IRAM PdBI beam (5.3'' x 4.6'') to test for resolved-out emission around companion #1.

recipe.goal: Search for additional CO(3-2) emitting sources in the field
recipe.method: Run SOFIA on the cleaned, natural-weighted data cube (without primary beam correction) using noise scaling by local standard deviation and the smooth + clip finder with median absolute deviation rms mode and a 5-sigma threshold. Complement with visual inspection of collapsed line maps.
key_parameters: noise scaling with standard deviation; smooth + clip with median absolute deviation rms mode; 5-sigma threshold; default merging; no source parametrisation

recipe.goal: Extract 1D spectra and fit CO(3-2) line profiles
recipe.method: Create integrated intensity (moment-0) maps of the sources, calculate the rms of the moment-0 maps, define extraction regions including line emission starting at the 2-sigma level, extract 1D spectra from the continuum-subtracted data cube (using the primary beam corrected cube for the companions), and fit single Gaussian line profiles.
key_parameters: aperture contour threshold = 2 sigma on moment-0 map

recipe.goal: Compute CO line luminosities and molecular gas masses
recipe.method: Convert velocity-integrated CO(3-2) line fluxes into CO(3-2) line luminosities L'_CO(3-2), convert to L'_CO(1-0) using assumed luminosity ratios r_32, and multiply by the CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha_CO.
assumptions: WMAP7 cosmology: H_0 = 70.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.272, Omega_Lambda = 0.728
r_32 = L'_CO(3-2)/L'_CO(1-0) = 0.97 for HzRG and 0.66 for companions
CO-H2 conversion factor = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 (with note that ~4 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 increases companion masses by a factor of 5)

recipe.goal: Identify Spitzer IRAC counterparts and estimate stellar mass of companion #1
recipe.method: Inspect archival Spitzer IRAC 3.6 um and 4.5 um images from the CARLA program at the positions of the ALMA CO detections, check completeness and colour criteria, and estimate an upper limit on the stellar mass of companion #1 from its rest-frame H-band (IRAC 3.6 um) luminosity.
key_parameters: CARLA completeness limits: 3.45 uJy at 3.6 um and 2.55 uJy at 4.5 um; colour criterion: [3.6]-[4.5] > -0.1

answer_key.quantity: North jet 100 GHz continuum flux density (S_100GHz)
South jet 100 GHz continuum flux density (S_100GHz)

evidence.loc: CO(3–2) line emission in TXS 0828+193 and companion #1
evidence.quote: Fitting a single Gaussian line to the CO(3–2) emission of the HzRG yields a FWHM of $616\pm138\,\rm km\,s^{-1}$ and a velocity integrated line flux $0.32\pm0.10\,\rm Jy\,km\,s^{-1}$.
In contrast to previous observations, we detect CO emission associated with the HzRG and derive a molecular gas mass of $(0.9\pm0.3)\times10^{10}\,\rm M_{\odot}$.

evidence.loc: CO(3–2) line emission in TXS 0828+193 and companion #1
evidence.quote: The CO emission of companion #1 has a FWHM of $635\pm150\,\rm km\,s^{-1}$ and a velocity integrated line flux of $0.23\pm0.07\,\rm Jy\,km\,s^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: Multi-wavelength properties of the companion candidates
evidence.quote: By assuming a mass-to-light ratio of 1, the IRAC $3.6\,\mu \rm m$ luminosity of the source puts an upper limit of $\sim 4.7\times10^{9}\,\rm M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ on its stellar mass (cite: 2003ApJS..149..289B).
The other two sources, hereafter companion #2 and #3, are located at projected distances of $29.9\,\rm arcsec$ ($\sim245\,\rm kpc$) and $21.6\,\rm arcsec$ ($\sim177\,\rm kpc$) from the HzRG.

score_reason: Single public ALMA Band 3 dataset (2015.1.00661.S) calibrated with the standard ALMA pipeline and imaged in CASA v5.4.0 with natural weighting and stated channel width (6 channels, 72.6 km/s), plus SOFIA source finding and simple Gaussian line fitting. Minor imaging and SOFIA kernel details are omitted, and 2-sigma moment-0 contour apertures introduce slight subjectivity.
rediscovery_reason: The raw ALMA data (2015.1.00661.S) are publicly available in the ALMA archive, the processing uses standard pipeline calibration, TCLEAN natural weighting, UVCONTSUB, and SOFIA, and all main results (100 GHz continuum fluxes, CO(3-2) integrated line fluxes, FWHMs, redshifts, luminosities, and gas masses in Table 1) are concrete numerical values suitable as an answer key.
